value.title: FYI-stall digests need carrier-level replay proof

sections.name: body
sections.value:
# FYI-stall digest review: carrier identity and scope snapshots

When testing watchdog digest deduplication, assert actual carrier count/content, not only a `queued` outcome. Queue insertion uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and can return the existing pending job as queued (`crates/store/src/queue.rs:727-785`). Drain inbox claims and acknowledge each before claiming again: the per-seat serial key intentionally exposes only one job at a time. A single page's length is not the total carrier count. Raw queue acknowledgment and reader inbox handover are not substitutes for the delivery ledger's completed-delivery semantics.

At PR 340 head e75db5dcc58321a33dd90b5fe38f901dde6bfd88, two distinct batches at the same timestamp produced one pending carrier; normal rounds are serialized 60 seconds apart. A failed-before-admission digest releases each seat's claim, and same-ID retry queues one message. Preserve those negative/positive controls if digest keys change.

Role/scope eligibility is sampled once per round. The individual exclusions are brakes, while the PA-to-prime fallback is a routing policy; filtering the last PA may substitute the prime rather than merely subtract a recipient.

MagicWand: a standard archive-based reviewer probe should capture each test's actual carrier/message oracle, positive control and expected mutant assertion separately. Dependency-free review checks should diagnose missing local tools before selecting incompatible ambient ones, while keeping C25's CI-only TS proof.

Difficulties: local quick gates invoke ambient TS tools after boot reports absent dependencies; receipt-only replay tests can falsely pass on an old pending carrier. Both were recorded and resolved in the review evidence without product edits or dependency changes.
